key_insight: Shared curvature enables Newton-based bilevel optimization beyond lower-level strong convexity, including settings with nonunique solutions and singular Hessians.
engineering_relevance: The methods target hyperparameter optimization, data reweighting, and meta-learning when classical hypergradient formulas may be unavailable.
method: Newton-based GALET exploits Hessian range structure under a positive spectral gap, avoiding GALET’s squared-Hessian multiplier system.
Newton-based BAMM uses a strongly convex aggregation model when the lower objective is convex and the upper objective is strongly convex in the lower variable.
GNBO unifies the shared-curvature structure of these methods and several existing Newton and quasi-Newton bilevel methods.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports convergence guarantees and improved complexity bounds over GALET and sl-BAMM under corresponding assumptions, plus evaluations on synthetic problems, data hyper-cleaning, and GPT-2 data reweighting.
watch_item: The guarantees remain assumption-dependent: removing lower-level strong convexity does not remove spectral-gap or other convexity requirements.
paper_title: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity
